inventions.definition: A typed Genome is the canonical form of a GSPL seed: $gst, $domain, $lineage, and a genes map of named Gene values.
inventions.founderIntent: A typed Genome is the canonical form of a GSPL seed. It carries $gst (schema version), $domain (one of 26), $lineage (operation + parents + generation + optional timestamp), and a genes map of named Gene values keyed by gene name.
inventions.problemSolved: Programs need a stable, addressable, hashable canonical representation.
risks: Schema drift if $gst version is bumped without a corresponding ADR
Ambiguity if gene names are duplicated across the 17-type inventory

inventions.definition: Empirically-derived initial inventory of 17 gene types: scalar, categorical, vector, expression, struct, array, graph, topology, temporal, regulatory, field, symbolic, quantum, gematria, resonance, dimensional, sovereignty.
inventions.founderIntent: The 17 gene types are the INITIAL STANDARD LIBRARY INVENTORY empirically derived by implementing 26 domain engines under spec/02. They are EXTENSIBLE per the EXTENSIBILITY PROTOCOL.
inventions.problemSolved: Composability requires a finite, type-tagged set of gene primitives with per-type (validate, mutate, crossover, distance, canonicalize) operators.
risks: Reading 17 as a closed set is denied by ADR-0004.

inventions.definition: A deterministic seedable RNG stack: SplitMix64 (seeding), xoshiro256** (state evolution), FNV-1a (genetic hashing), Box-Muller (Gaussian).
inventions.founderIntent: GSPL reproducibility requires every random decision to flow through a deterministic seedable RNG. The canon-foundation implementation uses SplitMix64 seeding, xoshiro256** state evolution, FNV-1a hashing, and Box-Muller Gaussian sampling.
inventions.problemSolved: Different OS, libm, or wall-clock must produce identical random outputs.
risks: Migration to a different PRNG family would break reproducibility of in-flight gseeds.

inventions.definition: The SHA-256 cryptographic hash function as defined in FIPS 180-4.
inventions.founderIntent: All content identifiers in GSPL sovereignty are SHA-256 of the JCS-canonical encoding of the object. The implementation is pure JS with NIST FIPS 180-4 test vectors pinned.
inventions.problemSolved: GSPL sovereignty requires a globally stable, collision-resistant content identifier.
risks: Quantum attacks on SHA-256 are not a near-term threat but are noted (ADR-0001).

inventions.definition: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme.
inventions.founderIntent: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785) is the substrate of GSPL content identity. The implementation follows the spec exactly with shortest-roundtrip number formatting, lex-sorted object keys, and UTF-16 surrogate pairs preserved.
inventions.problemSolved: Two equivalent JSON documents must hash to the same SHA-256 to be canonically equivalent.
risks: Library drift if a third-party JCS implementation differs from RFC 8785 in edge cases.

inventions.definition: The $lineage field of a Genome: operation, parents, generation, optional timestamp.
inventions.founderIntent: Every GSPL seed carries a $lineage block recording the operation that produced it, the parent gseeds, and the generation number. The lineage timestamp is deliberately normalized out of canonical hashes because timestamps would break reproducibility.
inventions.problemSolved: Reconstructing the history of a seed requires every gseed to know how it was produced.
risks: External tooling often mutates without writing a new $lineage.

inventions.definition: Per-gene-type operator suite: validate, mutate, crossover, distance, canonicalize.
inventions.founderIntent: Each gene type carries the same five canonical operators, satisfying the per-type property tests in spec/02. The 5-operator convention makes genetic composition closed under the inventory.
inventions.problemSolved: Genetic operations should compose uniformly without per-type special cases.
risks: Per-type operators that do not satisfy the per-type property tests are flagged by ADR-0004.

inventions.definition: Initial inventory of 26 reserved GSPL keywords: seed, breed, mutate, compose, evolve, grow, export, import, let, fn, if, else, match, for, while, return, true, false, null, type, trait, impl, where, gene, domain, signed.
inventions.founderIntent: The Initial Inventory of 26 reserved GSPL keywords. Additions are conservative because keywords change source-code meaning. EXTENSIBLE per the EXTENSIBILITY PROTOCOL.
inventions.problemSolved: A core language needs a stable, finite, parsimonious reserved-word set.
risks: Adding keywords can silently break existing source code.

inventions.definition: Recursive-descent parser producing the typed AST as defined in spec/04.
inventions.founderIntent: A recursive-descent parser over a 25+ node typed AST, layered atop the 26-keyword grammar. The parser is partial in canon-foundation; full coverage requires the canonical IR (deferred to Prompt 2).
inventions.problemSolved: A canonical parser makes source code reproducible across implementations.
risks: Edge cases (operator precedence, generics) are not fully exercised in canon-foundation tests.

inventions.definition: Typed Abstract Syntax Tree with at least 25 node kinds as defined in spec/04.
inventions.founderIntent: A typed AST with at least 25 node kinds forms the substrate of language interpretation and codegen.
inventions.problemSolved: A typed intermediate shape enables both interpretation and codegen, with type-aware diagnostics.
risks: AST drift between interpreters and codegen produces non-deterministic outputs.

inventions.definition: Tree-walking interpreter over the typed AST.
inventions.founderIntent: An AST interpreter executes a GSPL program by walking the AST and applying environment-scoped substitutions.
inventions.problemSolved: Reference execution semantics without committing to a particular compilation target.
risks: Interpreter and codegen may disagree on edge cases until a canonical semantics document exists.

inventions.definition: AST to ES2020 codegen pipeline emitting JavaScript modules.
inventions.founderIntent: A codegen pipeline that lowers a typed AST to ES2020 JavaScript for cross-language projection. Currently uses the typed AST as the de-facto IR.
inventions.problemSolved: Cross-language projection of GSPL programs to standard JavaScript runtimes.
risks: If a canonical IR is adopted, codegen must be retrofitted to consume it.

inventions.definition: A canonical GSPL IR is RESEARCH-REQUIRED; the references propose different IRs and no canonical choice is locked yet.
inventions.founderIntent: A canonical GSPL IR is researched but not adopted. The referenced allocations across paradigms vary. ADR-0008 records this as research-only until Prompt 2 finalizes a canonical IR shape.
inventions.problemSolved: Codegen, optimizer, and debugger would benefit from a unified IR.
risks: Without a canonical IR, codegen and interpreter drift; paradigms diverge.

inventions.definition: 8-phase tick cycle: intake, classify, bind, project, persist, validate, complete, idle.
inventions.founderIntent: The runtime ticks through eight ordered phases: intake, classify, bind, project, persist, validate, complete, idle. Each tick is deterministic given the seed and current knowledge version.
inventions.problemSolved: Runtime phases must be deterministic and reproducible across hosts.
risks: Adding phases would require a major version bump to the runtime contract.

inventions.definition: Eight algebraic effects: spawn, transform, observe, compose, dispose, audit, sign, broadcast. Algebraic semantics are RESEARCH.
inventions.founderIntent: Eight algebraic effects are planned: spawn, transform, observe, compose, dispose, audit, sign, broadcast. The cycle framework stubs each effect but the algebraic semantics remain research-only.
inventions.problemSolved: Programs need a stable, composable vocabulary for runtime side-effects without arbitrary I/O.
risks: Algebraic semantics not yet pinned; effect-channel drift is possible.

inventions.definition: Binary container for shipping and storing a Genome on disk.
inventions.founderIntent: A gseed file begins with the four-byte magic GSED, followed by a header that records content hash, schema version, and lineage. The format is content-addressed: two gseeds with the same content body and lineage are byte-identical.
inventions.problemSolved: A reproducible container format lets gseeds be checkpointed, shared, and reproduced byte-for-byte.
risks: Adding fields without bumping $gst version silently invalidates downstream readers.

inventions.definition: ECDSA P-256 signatures with deterministic RFC 6979 nonces over the SHA-256 content root of a gseed lineage.
inventions.founderIntent: Sovereignty is established by an ECDSA P-256 keypair whose verified signatures cover gseed lineage and a SHA-256 content root. Signatures are deterministic per RFC 6979 so different signatories produce identical signatures over the same input.
inventions.problemSolved: Programs must attest authorship and lineage integrity across hosts, in a universally portable key format.
risks: Non-deterministic nonces break reproducibility. ADHOC crypto is forbidden by ADR-0001.

inventions.definition: Seven structural axes: signed, typed, lineage-tracked, graph-structured, confidence-bearing, rollback-able, differentiable.
inventions.founderIntent: Seven structural axes that every GSPL surface satisfies: signed, typed, lineage-tracked, graph-structured, confidence-bearing, rollback-able, differentiable. Dropping any axis breaks the Next-Axis claim of the substrate.
inventions.problemSolved: Without a structural contract, every GSPL output shape drifts; surfaces diverge.
risks: Adding an axis would be a major canon change.

inventions.definition: Canonical CLI surface (validate, hash, seed, expand, sign, verify) for sovereign GSPL operations.
inventions.founderIntent: A canonical GSPL CLI with subcommands: gspl validate, gspl hash, gspl seed, gspl expand, gspl sign, gspl verify. The surface is adapted from paradigm-gspl-os and governed by ADR-0009.
inventions.problemSolved: A canonical CLI surface prevents tooling drift and undocumented command behavior.
risks: Adding CLI subcommands without an ADR would lock users into unstable command shapes.

inventions.definition: Vitest configuration and conventions for canonical testing.
inventions.founderIntent: All canon-related tests use Vitest and live in test/ directories inside each package. The framework hosts per-package property tests and the cross-package consistency tests.
inventions.problemSolved: A consistent test framework is required to host per-package test suites and the cross-package consistency tests.
risks: Test framework drift would invalidate the consistency tests that tie registry to ledgers.
